findings.body:
**A refusal (exit 2) writes nothing to stdout, but the docs promise one JSON artifact.**

`HOST-DEPLOY.md:179-181` says one JSON artifact goes to stdout, and that exit 2 means "refused before helper entry". This handler writes only to stderr. A caller that parses stdout gets an empty string for every refusal.

Doctrine I1 requires `{ "error": { kind, subcommand, message, exitCode } }` on stdout when an error has no result. A refusal needs a machine-readable reason, so emit that object.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
     except Refused as exc:
         print("refused: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        print(json.dumps({"error": {"kind": "refused", "subcommand": args.operation,
+                                    "message": str(exc), "exitCode": 2}},
+                         indent=2, sort_keys=True))
         return 2
```
</details>
As per coding guidelines, "Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed."
findings.title: A refusal (exit 2) writes nothing to stdout, but the docs promise one JSON artifact.

findings.body:
**`health` reports `healthy: true` without gating on receipt readability.**

`HOST-DEPLOY.md:240-242` says receipt readability is a distinct check. It also says "advancement alone is not acceptance". The module docstring (lines 22-25) says the same.

`health_observation` counts readable receipts. The count is `receipt_sample["readable"]`, and it also includes directories that have no `meta.json`. `two_slot_health` (line 463) never reads it. The result is that corrupt `meta.json` files produce `healthy: true` and exit 0.

Count `meta.json` files that fail to parse, and fail health when any exist. Do not count directories without `meta.json`, because those can be in-flight starts.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-                try:
-                    json.loads(meta.read_text())
-                    readable += 1
-                except (ValueError, OSError):
-                    pass
-        receipt_sample = {"sampled": len(entries[:10]), "readable": readable}
+                try:
+                    json.loads(meta.read_text())
+                    readable += 1
+                except (ValueError, OSError):
+                    unreadable += 1
+        receipt_sample = {"sampled": len(entries[:10]), "readable": readable,
+                          "unreadable": unreadable}
```

Also initialize `unreadable = 0` next to `readable = 0` at line 430. Then gate the result:

```diff
-    return {"healthy": True, "observations": [first, second]}
+    if any((obs.get("receipts") or {}).get("unreadable") for obs in (first, second)):
+        return {"healthy": False, "reason": "unreadable receipt metadata",
+                "observations": [first, second]}
+    return {"healthy": True, "observations": [first, second]}
```
</details>






Also applies to: 463-463
findings.title: `health` reports `healthy: true` without gating on receipt readability.

findings.body:
**Run snapshot filter drivers only under an explicit safety rule.**

The admission safety list at `tree-snapshots.md:74-75` disables snapshot hooks, external diff/textconv commands, replacement refs, and inherited Git config. It does not name filter drivers. Launch checkout then runs a runner-configured required smudge filter that the snapshot's `.gitattributes` activates (`tree-snapshots.md:81-83`). That filter is an external command, and it receives snapshot content as input. The doc does not state that this execution is bounded, screened, or refused, so an untrusted snapshot can run that command before the review starts.

Specify one of these behaviors in the protocol:
- Refuse launch when snapshot attributes activate any filter driver that the runner does not explicitly allow.
- Or document the allowed filter set and the input it receives, and state why that input is safe.

The current text does not state either behavior.
findings.title: Run snapshot filter drivers only under an explicit safety rule.
